RuntimeError: AgentV SDK is unavailable; run npm ci in the checkout or set AGENTV_RUNNER

harness_repair.diagnosis: This session's fresh sandbox checkout (a new remote execution container, distinct from the sandbox that produced the 2026-08-03 c1/c2 torch/NODE_OPTIONS fixes already on main) had never run `npm ci`, so evaluate_model.py --ship-gates crashed in publish_model_evaluation with the same 'AgentV SDK is unavailable' error the c2 doc already covers -- but only after both arms had already spent their full training wall (4.12s and 3.72s of the ~180s cycle cap). `npm ci` itself failed once with 'node: --import tsx is not allowed in NODE_OPTIONS' because the host shell exports a NODE_OPTIONS this Node build rejects for the npm process itself (a different exposure than the already-fixed bridge_utils.sanitized_node_env() subprocess spawns, which only sanitize env for node processes *launched by* Python); `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm ci` (the exact invocation scripts/setup_dev_env.sh already uses) succeeded. The remaining gap: the continuous driver only discovered the missing SDK after training, misspending wall budget and giving `harness_failure:...:experiment_failed` per arm instead of a single fast, correctly-attributed preflight failure.
harness_repair.fix_summary: Added slm_training.evals.agentv.ensure_agentv_available(repo_root) -- a thin, testable wrapper around the existing _agentv_runtime() resolution -- and call it at the top of scripts.run_autotrain_continuous.run_cycle() before git sync, so a cold checkout missing the AgentV SDK fails in milliseconds with the existing actionable 'run npm ci' message instead of after a full wasted train step. No change to _agentv_runtime()'s resolution logic or the NODE_OPTIONS sanitization landed in the prior cycle; this is a preflight-timing fix only.
